inflammation.description: Early healing phase: redness, swelling and warmth around the wound are normal.
inflammation.duration: Typically lasts 1–5 days after injury or surgery.
care_tips: Keep the wound clean and dry.
Do not scratch or rub the area.
Mild swelling and redness are expected.

normal_healing.description: The wound is progressing through the healing process normally.
normal_healing.duration: Can last from a few days to several weeks depending on wound size.
care_tips: Avoid exposing the wound to direct sunlight.
Stay hydrated and eat a balanced diet to support healing.
Watch for any sudden changes in appearance.

fully healed.description: The wound has closed and healed completely.
fully healed.duration: Scar maturation can continue for up to 2 years.
care_tips: Moisturize the scar area to improve texture.
Use SPF 30+ sunscreen on the scar when exposed to sunlight.
Gentle massage can help soften the scar tissue.

infected.description: Signs of infection are present: increased redness, swelling, warmth, pus or fever.

dehiscence.description: The wound has reopened: the edges have separated after surgical closure.
